paragraph_screen.baseline_text: Carryover is an established concern in automated laboratories. AutoFSP reports chemical measurements of batch contamination and discusses flushing in automated catalyst synthesis [1]. PANDA includes fluid-handling validation and cross-contamination control in a platform for electrodeposited polymer films [2]. These studies motivate the problem but do not calibrate the composition-retention parameters used here. More recently, the VERID preprint demonstrates diagnosis of a wall-film carryover artifact using laboratory state and targeted physical experiments [5]. Therefore the research opportunity cannot rest on observing that laboratories remember previous experiments.

paragraph_screen.baseline_text: We investigate when preparation history prevents a fresh-response conclusion, when repetition removes the ambiguity and when washing or independent preparation can improve confirmation under a cost cap. We evaluate the planner alongside strong simple controls. A preceding synthetic benchmark is preserved because it supplies a consequential negative finding: its adaptive information-per-cost heuristic did not demonstrate superiority over repetition using the same history model. The resulting paper is a methods and failure-analysis study with a real-data application, not a report of a newly synthesized material.

paragraph_screen.baseline_text: History-aware modeling is established. Roussel and Hanuka jointly represent hysteresis and response in Bayesian regression and optimization [3]. Our target is narrower: the mean fresh-preparation response of one recipe frozen after a discovery campaign. Conditioning on the discovery record separates that target from subsequent confirmation noise. It does not remove selection bias from reused discovery observations, which is why the bounded confirmation intervals use newly collected confirmation measurements only.

If joint physical bounds are valid with probability at least 1 − δ, combining calibration and confirmation errors yields a lower coverage bound of 1 − α − δ. This requires an actual calibration statement. A global L proved for a fitted emulator does not bound the difference between that emulator and the true material. Nor does the largest observed slope in a finite dataset provide an upper bound on unseen material sensitivity. These restrictions determine the scope of every guarantee reported here.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The planner considers routine candidate assays, candidate assays after one or three washes and independent fresh candidate assays. It enumerates feasible nonnegative action counts under a fixed budget, with at least two measurements. Every included observation has equal weight. For fixed counts, stronger washes should precede weaker washes and routine repeats. To prove this, compare two adjacent shared-line actions with retained-fraction bounds rₐ ≤ rᵦ and common replacement lower bound λmin. Their summed bias-bound difference after swapping the order is:
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The final state-distance bound is the same product in either order, so later terms do not change. Repeated adjacent swaps establish the optimal order for those fixed counts. Fresh actions have zero preparation bias and do not change the shared state, making their placement irrelevant to this final-width objective. The code places them last. A block of n identical shared actions contributes LrD(1 − qⁿ)/(1 − q), where q = 1 − λmin(1 − r). Enumeration then selects the count tuple minimizing Equation (6). Ties favor lower cost, fewer fresh assays, fewer washes and more routine assays in that order.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: This is an exact optimum within the declared finite class of fixed, candidate-only, equally weighted schedules. It does not optimize over outcome-adaptive policies, unequal weighting, discarded burn-in or arbitrary experimental interventions. Minimum worst-case width also need not imply minimum realized estimation error or maximum acceptance yield. Those are separate empirical outcomes. The fixed tail-average control is therefore retained even though it lies outside the planner’s optimality class. At equal routine and fresh costs, all-fresh measurements weakly dominate the menu in certified width: they maximize affordable sample count while contributing zero preparation bias.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The primary OPV emulator is a degree-three standard Bernstein polynomial on the four-component simplex. For degree p, the coefficient vector contains every multi-index of total degree p in the standard multinomial Bernstein basis. Appendix A gives the basis and derivative explicitly. A global L1 Lipschitz upper bound for this mathematical polynomial is:
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The factor one half follows because composition changes sum to zero: the dual norm on simplex tangent directions is half the range of gradient components. Bernstein basis weights are nonnegative and sum to one, so the largest adjacent coefficient difference bounds the gradient range everywhere. Integrating along a straight simplex segment proves Equation (8). The certificate is recomputed from the final fitted coefficients and rounded conservatively. Only scalar Lcert is exposed to the bounded policies. The coefficients, clean response and simulator state remain private to the simulator and scoring code. This certificate establishes mathematical regularity of the emulator, not physical validation of an OPV formulation.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Langner et al. measured photostability of four-component organic-photovoltaic blends after 18 hours of approximately one-sun illumination in ambient air [11]. The response is relative spectral absorbance loss of films, not device power-conversion efficiency. We retrieved the original authors’ experimental workbook at a pinned repository commit and retained its exact bytes and SHA256. System 01 contains P3HT, PBQ-QF, PCBM and oIDTBR. System 02 contains P3HT, PTB7-Th, PCBM and oIDTBR. Each sheet contains 1,041 high-throughput measurements representing 1,021 unique composition groups. Each system also contains two self-driving campaigns with 60 formulations and two measured samples per formulation. The extracted dataset therefore contains 2,562 measured responses, including 240 paired formulations.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Composition values are mass fractions summing to one despite the workbook’s wt.-% headings; they are not divided by 100 again. Repeated compositions are grouped only for emulator fitting, retaining all original responses separately. Negative measured losses are retained. The two systems share some observations on the zero-second-donor face and are not independent external replications. A cross-check against processed Olympus copies identified differences between descriptive metadata and original numeric column/system identity. We use the original workbook headers corroborated by the source supporting information, preserve the cross-check and do not silently substitute repository aliases for chemical identities.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The paired-measurement analysis includes all 240 pairs and uses the illustrative loss threshold 0.10. It tabulates both-pass, each direction of disagreement and both-fail outcomes. Sample 1 and Sample 2 are source labels. They do not establish temporal order, independent fresh preparation or a controlled carryover intervention. The analysis is descriptive for this finite dataset; no population confidence interval is attached because adaptive selection, shared compositions and undocumented preparation dependence prevent an independent random-sample interpretation. A disagreement is not a known false acceptance because the true mean response is unobserved.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: For each system, the 1,021 composition groups are partitioned using the fixed seed 880001 into 715 training, 152 validation and 154 test groups. All replicate measurements remain in the same group. The four pure vertices are assigned to training before the remaining split, so the test assessment does not evaluate extrapolation to unseen pure vertices. The cubic Bernstein family is fixed before evaluation. Ridge strengths 10⁻⁶, 10⁻⁴, 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10 are compared using validation mean absolute error. Ties prefer stronger regularization. The selected value is 0.01 in both systems. A train-plus-validation refit is followed by one held-out fidelity assessment. We do not retune the model after viewing its test errors.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: A separately fixed continuous piecewise-affine Delaunay interpolant provides an emulator sensitivity. It uses composition-group means and retains sharp local variation. Its fivefold group validation excludes and counts held-out points outside each training hull rather than silently extrapolating. The full-data interpolant covers the simplex because all pure vertices are present. Each cell’s gradient yields a global sensitivity certificate. Its validation partition and coverage differ from the cubic model’s held-out test, so raw error scores are not used to claim a matched superiority comparison. Both emulators remain approximations to published measurements. Artificial carryover added to either model is a controlled simulation, not an observed OPV process.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The first benchmark uses a ternary mixture response with a randomly generated quadratic surface and controlled nonlinear stresses. A stateless Bayesian quadratic upper-confidence-bound optimizer starts with eight randomly selected untested recipes and performs 24 discovery assays in total on a 0.1 simplex grid. The tested nominal recipe with the highest final posterior mean is frozen. The confirmation budget is 16 units, with routine or conditioning assays costing 1, each wash 0.5 and a fresh assay 4 in the principal setting. The primary target is a dimensionless fresh response of at least 0.85. These response and cost scales are synthetic.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: A history model averages 24 retained-fraction and wash-retention particles, using Gaussian Bayesian linear regression in six quadratic Bernstein features. The adaptive policy scores each action by the squared posterior covariance between the fresh target and prospective observation, divided by observation variance and action cost. This is a moment-based linear-projection heuristic, not exact information gain. Crucially, a history-repeat control uses the same posterior model while repeatedly preparing the frozen candidate. Other controls include candidate repetition, sequence repetition, random predecessors, one or three washes, fixed history-model interventions, fresh-only measurement and a cost-blind adaptive ablation. Every policy receives the same budget cap and continues while an action remains affordable; discrete action costs can produce different realized spending. First posterior-threshold crossings are descriptive rather than a tested stopping guarantee.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The frozen design contains 400 campaign seeds per scenario across 12 scenarios and 10 policies: 4,800 scenario–seed campaigns and 48,000 policy runs. Seeds are reused across scenarios to support controlled comparisons. They are not 4,800 independent material response surfaces. Each individual scenario has 400 independent seed draws. The evaluation includes no or weak carryover, ineffective washing, persistent memory, nonlinear response, changed intervention costs, off-grid parameters and severe retention. Results from this first evaluation are preserved unchanged. The later OPV extension was designed after its negative comparative finding and is described with that chronology, not as an externally preregistered study.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The extension uses four-component 0.1-grid nominal candidates whose total donor fraction lies between 1/6 and 5/6, matching the source study’s donor-to-acceptor eligibility range [11]. Discovery uses 12 random starts and 32 total stateless quadratic UCB assays. For each system, scenario and seed, every method receives the same discovery record and frozen candidate; its simulated line starts from the same hidden state. There is no filtering for apparently successful discoveries. The score threshold is 0.90 and the confirmation budget is 32. Independent Gaussian observation noise has assumed σ = 0.03; this is not estimated from the source paired measurements.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Eight simulated preparation scenarios cover zero, trace, low, moderate and high carryover, ineffective washing, moderate persistent memory and a strongly persistent stress. Retained fractions include 0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.10 and 0.40. The persistent scenarios use replacement fractions 0.45 and 0.05. All are specified simulation parameters. Bounded methods receive the same externally assumed envelopes for retention, wash efficacy and replacement, plus the scalar emulator certificate. They receive no clean-response or latent-state oracle. Model-based controls may restrict their particles using the same retention envelopes, but their quadratic and immediate-memory assumptions can still be misspecified.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Thirteen methods are compared: sequence repeat, candidate repeat, a fixed four-assay burn-in/tail average, one wash per assay, fresh-only, history-model repeat, the original adaptive heuristic, an adaptive ablation without conditioning actions and five bounded variants comprising repeat, tail average, one-wash, fresh-only and the finite-menu planner. Bounded variants use Equation (6) at the final planned sample count. The primary design comprises 200 seeds per system and scenario, two systems and eight scenarios. The 3,200 scenario–system–seed campaigns produce 41,600 policy runs. Per-case paired uncertainty respects the shared campaign design; pooled rows are not treated as independent replications.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The protocol separately declares sensitivities on the first 100 evaluation seeds for low and high carryover in both systems: the piecewise-affine emulator, broad but valid preparation bounds, resampled empirical replicate contrasts and equal fresh/routine costs. Empirical contrast noise uses symmetric signed half-differences of measured sample pairs while retaining large deviations. It is an assumption stress, not a validated noise distribution for future OPV experiments. The same Gaussian cutoff remains in that stress deliberately, so its theorem does not apply. Deterministic budget diagnostics vary budgets 8, 16, 32 and 64 and fresh costs 1, 2, 4 and 8. The complete scenario parameters, code hashes, chronology and run logs accompany the notebook.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: For each case, we report true candidate prevalence, false acceptance per campaign, true acceptance yield, false rejection, unresolved outcomes, error among accepted candidates, estimation error and cost. Bounded methods additionally report interval coverage and width. Binary-rate intervals use Wilson 95% intervals. Differences use 5,000 paired campaign bootstrap resamples. These intervals quantify simulation uncertainty within a case; they are not multiplicity-adjusted and do not imply cross-platform generalization. Zero observed errors are accompanied by finite uncertainty rather than described as zero risk. Equal outcome counts or intervals spanning zero are not interpreted as equivalence.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The original paired measurements contain 10 threshold disagreements among 240 pairs (4.17%). PBQ-QF has six disagreements among 120 pairs and PTB7-Th has four among 120 pairs. Across both systems, 100 Sample 1 measurements meet the criterion; six of their paired Sample 2 measurements do not. These observations establish decision-boundary disagreement in the retrieved data. They do not estimate a carryover effect, a false-discovery rate or the probability that an independently prepared recipe will fail.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Variation is heterogeneous. The median absolute paired difference is 0.00618 for PBQ-QF and 0.00559 for PTB7-Th, while the largest differences are 0.13871 and 0.36165. The large PTB7-Th difference is retained in both the descriptive analysis and empirical-contrast sensitivity. A summary based only on central differences would not describe these extremes. The source does not identify which contributions arise from preparation, measurement, aging or other variation. The paired analysis therefore motivates confirmation without assigning its mechanism.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: In the strong-carryover synthetic case, adaptive confirmation accepts 229 truly valid recipes compared with 235 for history-model repetition. The paired yield difference is −1.5 percentage points, with a 95% bootstrap interval from −3.25 to +0.25 points. This does not demonstrate an advantage for the adaptive policy. Ordinary candidate repetition also performs well because the repeated composition flushes the line. Comparing the adaptive method only against sequence repetition would have overstated the contribution by omitting the more informative simple controls.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Under the nonlinear stress, sequence repetition makes 36 false acceptances in 400 campaigns: 9.0% (Wilson 95% interval 6.57–12.21%). Adaptive confirmation and history-model repetition each make zero false acceptances, but the adaptive method makes two false rejections and has mean absolute error 0.01167 versus 0.00895. The paired error difference is +0.00272 (95% bootstrap interval 0.00174–0.00376), favoring the simpler method on this metric. Zero false acceptances in 400 trials still permits an approximate 0.95% Wilson upper limit. In the severe-retention case, sequence repetition makes 37 false acceptances and ordinary candidate repetition makes six; history-model repetition and the adaptive method make none in the observed campaigns.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: These results support a mechanism-based explanation rather than a universal ranking. When repeated candidate assays quickly remove residue, they both improve physical preparation and collect inexpensive information about the target. Conditioning actions can reintroduce a noncandidate predecessor while consuming budget. The original covariance utility uses immediate predictive covariance and does not value future state changes. Its inference can also be affected by model misspecification. The same-model comparison isolates the value of intervention choice from the value of fitting a history-aware response model. It does not establish that every sophisticated policy must fail.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Held-out mean absolute errors are 0.04390 and 0.05097 for PBQ-QF and PTB7-Th, with R² values 0.6062 and 0.4849. These are moderate predictive fidelities relative to a loss criterion of 0.10. A mathematically valid emulator interval can therefore be uninformative about the real formulation without an additional model-discrepancy bound. The primary L1 certificates are 1.66314 and 1.88188. They are not fitted from the subsequent policy outcomes.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The alternative piecewise-affine model has fivefold validation coverage of 1,008 of 1,021 composition groups in each system; 13 points outside the corresponding training hull are explicitly excluded. On the covered points, MAE is 0.02880 for PBQ-QF and 0.03714 for PTB7-Th. Its full-model L1 bounds are much larger: 65.66965 and 50.64746. These large bounds are retained in the sensitivity experiment rather than reduced to obtain favorable confirmation. The different holdout schemes preclude a direct matched predictive-superiority claim.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The completed extension contains 62,400 policy runs: 41,600 primary runs and 20,800 predefined sensitivity runs. The primary cases include 9 of 16 system–scenario combinations in which all 200 frozen candidates qualify under the cubic emulator. These easy cases can compare precision and cost but cannot estimate false acceptance conditional on an invalid recipe. Across all primary cases, valid-candidate counts range from 26 to 200 of 200. The fixed criterion and every campaign are retained; no outcome-dependent threshold is introduced.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: A post-run audit finds negative predicted mean loss for all 200 selected candidates in each PBQ-QF no-, trace- and low-carryover case and for 180 of 200 in the PTB7-Th no-carryover case. These unclipped cubic-model predictions help explain the easy-case prevalence; they do not establish corresponding physical stability. Negative observed changes also exist in the source data, so sign alone does not identify an impossible measurement.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: With high carryover and effective washing, the planner selects two three-wash assays followed by 27 routine candidate assays. Its radius is 0.01251 for PBQ-QF and 0.01272 for PTB7-Th, compared with 0.02079 for eight fresh-only assays at the same budget. It accepts 190 and 194 truly valid candidates, versus 183 and 186 for fresh-only. The paired yield gains are +3.5 percentage points (95% interval +1.0 to +6.5) and +4.0 points (+1.0 to +7.0). Against fixed burn-in/tail repetition the gains are only +0.5 points (0 to +1.5) and +1.0 points (0 to +2.5). These results support a conditional efficiency benefit against costly fresh-only measurement, not dominance over strong repetition.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Ineffective washing reverses that ranking. The planner selects fresh-only, while the fixed tail control accepts six more valid recipes in each system: a planner-minus-tail difference of −3.0 percentage points with paired 95% intervals −6.0 to −0.5. Tail averaging is outside the planner’s equally weighted all-observation class and can have a smaller interval. This counterexample is retained because it identifies a concrete limit of the restricted optimization claim.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: With replacement fraction λ = 0.45, the planner again selects fresh-only. The bounded tail control accepts 64 of 200 PBQ-QF campaigns and nine of 200 PTB7-Th campaigns; planner/fresh-only accept 175 and 192. These gains reflect avoiding an overly conservative shared-line tail bound, not an advantage over the fresh-only baseline. At λ = 0.05, the bounded tail rule remains unresolved in all 200 campaigns for each system. A valid bound can therefore be practically uninformative. The correct response is to report its lack of resolution rather than interpret abstention as successful discovery.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The strongly persistent PTB7-Th stress contains 26 truly valid candidates among 200. The quadratic immediate-memory model is misspecified for this case. History-model repetition makes 10 false acceptances and the adaptive heuristic makes 12, corresponding to 5.0% and 6.0% of all campaigns. The planner and fresh-only rule each make zero observed false acceptances while accepting 17 valid candidates. Zero of 200 has a Wilson 95% upper limit of approximately 1.88%, so it is not evidence of zero error probability. This stress supports the need to distinguish posterior confidence from a conditional frequentist decision guarantee.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Observed coverage does not uniformly reach its nominal value in the finite simulation. Fixed tail averaging covers 183 of 200 targets (91.5%) in the no-carryover case, with Wilson 95% interval 86.81–94.63%; its upper limit is below 95%. Fresh-only covers 186 of 200 (93.0%; interval 88.59–95.78%). The same common Gaussian draws produce repeated fluctuations in several cases. These finite results are preserved rather than erased by changing seeds or enlarging the sample after inspection. The mathematical conditional guarantee follows from the stated Gaussian model and bias envelope; the simulation must not be described as a universal empirical coverage validation. The accompanying audit directly checks noise normalization and discarded-prefix indexing.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The predefined sensitivities expose different limitations. Broad but valid apparatus bounds cause the planner to use fresh-only and make the bounded tail rule unresolved in every one of the four 100-campaign cases. With the less smooth Delaunay emulator and high carryover, the planner also chooses fresh-only; one false acceptance occurs in the PBQ-QF case. At equal fresh/routine cost, the planner selects 32 fresh assays and exactly matches the fresh-only interval in all four cases, as the width objective requires. The empirical-contrast-noise stress retains observed extreme pair differences; its fixed Gaussian interval has no theorem-backed coverage under that noise law, regardless of its observed coverage. No parameter, family or scenario was changed to improve these results.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: An additional intervention is useful when it reduces preparation ambiguity enough to compensate for the measurements it displaces. Equations (4)–(6) separate two mechanisms: preparation bias and sampling noise. At low retention or rapid replacement, routine repetition can make the bias negligible while preserving sample count. With persistent memory, useful washing can reduce the retained fraction early in a sequence. With broad bounds, weak cleaning or a highly sensitive response model, a direct fresh measurement may offer the only tight preparation guarantee. If fresh preparation has the same marginal cost as a routine assay, the certificate favors fresh-only. These are model-conditional statements with explicit countercases, not recommendations for an uncalibrated laboratory.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The preparation reference is part of the scientific claim. A mixture that benefits from residue may reveal a useful composition; it should be recorded and independently prepared as that composition before being credited to the nominal recipe. Likewise, an unresolved confirmation is an informative outcome when the available evidence cannot separate a near-threshold target from preparation or measurement variation. Reporting only accepted candidates would conceal this tradeoff. The proposed method makes uncertainty and resource assumptions explicit but cannot replace chemical characterization or experimental replication.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: AutoFSP provides a concrete but separate physical example [1]. Its published contamination table reports six element-specific measurements across four batches, from 0.016 to 0.122 mol% relative to the main phase. The authors describe the quantities as near analytical quantification limits. One cleaning cycle is reported to take approximately 30 seconds and the standard sequence uses three cycles; 90 seconds is therefore an arithmetic duration for that sequence. The paper also reports campaign preparation/processing times and parallel operations. These published observations support the practical relevance of carryover and cleaning burden. They do not establish the OPV emulator’s retained-mixture mass fraction ρ, wash factor η or marginal fresh-preparation cost.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Element contamination in a catalyst is not interchangeable with a residual-mixture fraction in a photovoltaic formulation. Converting between them requires the predecessor composition, assay calibration, transfer mechanism and mass balance. Likewise, summed cleaning durations need not equal marginal wall-clock delay when steps run in parallel. For the actual OPV platform, the source reports formation of 96 films in 22 minutes and also gives drying, annealing and 18-hour aging durations [11]. Batch throughput does not identify the incremental cost of an independent fresh preparation. We transcribe these reported quantities with units and source locations but keep them outside parameter calibration for the simulation. The absence of matched OPV preparation-history and cost records remains a material evidence gap.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: A proposed validation design would select two candidate compositions whose preliminary independent fresh measurements lie on opposite sides of the photostability criterion. It would combine these with three contrasting predecessors and three washing conditions: zero, one and three washes. An independent fresh condition is added for each candidate. Six independently prepared specimens per cell, each with its own target assay, give 2 × (3 × 3 + 1) × 6 = 120 target assays in the confirmation grid, plus charged predecessor preparations and separate candidate-selection calibration. This is a proposed calibration pilot, not a completed experiment or a justified final power calculation. A subsequent sample-size decision should use pilot uncertainty and the smallest practically important confirmation difference.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The pilot should record commanded and chemically measured composition where a validated composition-sensitive assay is available, including detection and quantification limits. Preparation chronology, shared-line identity, wash operations, day, substrate and aging block should remain linked to each outcome. Randomization within feasible blocks must preserve the intended predecessor relationship. Operator time, elapsed preparation time, material consumption and waste should be recorded separately. Since aging can be parallelized, fresh preparation should not automatically be assigned the full aging time as incremental cost. Separate calibration and confirmation runs would allow estimated instrument bounds to be assessed before the final decision rule is applied.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: This design still needs apparatus-specific chemical and statistical decisions. A physical sensitivity bound may be local to a restricted candidate neighborhood rather than global over the entire composition simplex. A largest observed slope is insufficient as an upper bound. Composition-dependent noise, systematic assay drift and morphology-mediated history may invalidate the simple model. Those possibilities should be tested or represented in expanded bias bounds. The current computational package supplies an executable method and falsifiable measurement plan; it does not report that these laboratory steps have occurred.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The primary limitations are substantive. The real dataset lacks the preparation histories needed for causal carryover estimation. The fitted emulators have moderate held-out fidelity and their mathematical certificates do not certify actual materials. The assumed physical bounds are provided to the policies, which favors calibrated methods relative to an uninstrumented laboratory. The principal noise model is independent Gaussian with known scale. Only one frozen candidate is confirmed per campaign; repeated searches for a favorable candidate would require a separate multiple-candidate error budget. The simplex mass-balance model omits selective adsorption, chemical transformation and morphology-dependent effects.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: The evaluation is also limited by design. Two OPV systems share some source observations. Reused seeds create controlled comparisons rather than independent evidence across every scenario. The finite-menu planner is not a general adaptive optimum. The initial active heuristic is one model-based strategy, so its failure cannot establish the impossibility of useful active confirmation. The broad-bound and empirical-noise sensitivities are part of a declared extension but not external validation. No physical laboratory trials, independent-team replication, exhaustive novelty search or journal acceptance assessment has been completed. These limits are compatible with a useful computational contribution but prevent a claim of validated autonomous materials discovery.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Preparation history changes which response a nominal recipe can support. A finite transcript away from the fresh target can leave its performance ambiguous; quantitative response and residual-state bounds make that ambiguity explicit. Under a stated contraction model, repetition naturally reduces history effects, explaining why strong simple controls can outperform an intervention heuristic. A restricted preparation planner can minimize a conditional final interval width by placing stronger washes first and enumerating feasible action counts. Published OPV measurements anchor the application and reveal real decision-boundary disagreement, while their missing history records prevent a causal carryover interpretation. The completed computations support a transparent confirmation framework and a scoped failure analysis. Establishing physical usefulness requires measured preparation history, credible calibration bounds and actual marginal costs on a materials platform.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Assume the finite data satisfy |yᵢ − yⱼ| ≤ L‖zᵢ − zⱼ‖. Define g₋(x) = maxᵢ[yᵢ − L‖zᵢ − x‖] and g₊(x) = minᵢ[yᵢ + L‖zᵢ − x‖]. Each constituent cone is L-Lipschitz. The finite maximum or minimum remains L-Lipschitz. At a sampled point zⱼ, pairwise consistency makes g₋(zⱼ) = g₊(zⱼ) = yⱼ. Any compatible f must lie between these envelopes by the Lipschitz inequality. Both endpoints at x* are therefore attained. Their convex combinations interpolate the same data and remain L-Lipschitz, proving sharpness of Equation (2). The result is an application of established extension theory [12], not a claim that the present preparation problem introduces that theorem.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: If simultaneous response bands ℓᵢ ≤ f(zᵢ) ≤ uᵢ are available and at least one L-Lipschitz function satisfies them, the analogous lower envelope maxᵢ[ℓᵢ − L‖zᵢ − x‖] and upper envelope minᵢ[uᵢ + L‖zᵢ − x‖] are feasible and attain the target endpoints. Feasibility is essential; incompatible bands cannot be repaired by silently returning a point estimate. Hidden-position upper bounds give valid but generally nonsharp envelopes. They ignore dependencies among positions implied by one common state trajectory.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Let Z be the finite set of actual queried compositions and suppose x* is not in Z. Choose r smaller than the positive distance from x* to Z. A smooth ambient bump supported within radius r can be normalized to equal one at x*. Given a compatible smooth f₀, the functions f₀ + Δb agree at every queried composition but have different fresh-target values. Restricting the ambient function to the simplex also covers a boundary target. Offsets on opposite sides of the criterion establish underdetermination in an unrestricted smooth class. If response-range constraints are imposed, the offsets must remain feasible; the opposite-conclusion claim requires a threshold in the allowed range. The construction is conditional on a finite transcript and does not assert equality of every possible randomized-design distribution.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: Substitute zₜ − x* = rₜ(hₜ₋₁ − x*) into the state update to obtain Equation (3). Its nonnegative multiplier is increasing in rₜ and decreasing in λₜ. The supplied bounds therefore imply Equation (4) by induction. Summing the resulting geometric sequence after b excluded observations gives Equation (5). This derivation makes the failure boundary explicit: when the worst-case contraction is one, the geometric sum has its limiting value m and the mean preparation bound need not shrink. A fresh action resets the target measurement’s bias, not the shared-line state.
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: For a fixed confirmation plan, write Ȳₙ − θ = b̄ₙ + ε̄ₙ with |b̄ₙ| ≤ B̄ₙ. Under independent Gaussian noise, P(|ε̄ₙ| ≤ z₁₋α/₂σ/√n) = 1 − α. The triangle inequality proves Equation (6). A false accept or false reject implies that the interval misses θ, hence the conditional wrong-decision probability is at most α. This argument is uniform over every bias sequence satisfying the stated envelope, but it does not estimate the envelope’s physical validity. Bias-aware inference has established precedents [13].
claims.qualification: Evidence supports the paragraph within its stated assumptions and exclusions.

claims.statement: For predictable actions with conditionally σ-sub-Gaussian errors, the exponential-moment bound yields a two-sided failure probability at most α/T at each sample count for radius σ√{2 log(2T/α)/n}. A union bound over n = 1,…,T yields simultaneous coverage. If a data-dependent contiguous tail can be selected from a horizon T, there are M = T(T + 1)/2 windows; replacing T by M and using each window’s own sample count and mean bias bound covers them simultaneously. Such corrections are not attached to the fixed-final primary experiment. Sharper time-uniform constructions may improve efficiency [10].

claims.statement: Preparation history can make the material measured in an autonomous campaign differ from its recorded recipe. We study confirmation of one frozen recipe under independent fresh preparation. A finite-data analysis distinguishes underdetermination without quantitative regularity from sharp response envelopes under a known Lipschitz bound. A mass-balance memory model yields a contraction-based preparation-bias bound and a conditional fixed-final confidence interval. An exchange argument establishes stronger-wash-first ordering for fixed action counts; enumeration minimizes interval width within a restricted equally weighted preparation menu. We reanalyze original organic-photovoltaic measurements, finding 10 threshold disagreements among 240 paired formulations at an illustrative absorbance-loss criterion. These observations do not establish carryover causality. A preserved synthetic benchmark contains 48,000 policy runs and does not demonstrate superiority of an adaptive heuristic over same-model repetition. A separate extension contains 62,400 runs using two measured-data-informed response emulators. In high-carryover cases, the planner improves true-acceptance yield over costly fresh-only measurement by 3.5 and 4.0 percentage points, but loses 3.0 points to fixed burn-in/tail repetition when washing is ineffective. Strong persistent-memory stress produces 12 false acceptances in 200 campaigns for the misspecified adaptive model. Finite observed coverage also falls below nominal 95% in some controls. Emulator test errors are moderate and its certificates do not certify physical materials. The contribution is a reproducible conditional confirmation framework with explicit efficiency and failure boundaries; platform-specific carryover, response bounds and marginal costs still require experimental validation.
